subject.title: fix: Node allowlist writeback can restore revoked exec approvals

question: Should execution-side exec approval writeback land as locked reload-and-merge against the latest file, or should maintainers require original-snapshot CAS/skipping when the approvals file changed after policy evaluation?
rationale: Both designs prevent stale whole-file restoration, but they differ on whether a pending allow-always decision may merge into a file that an admin changed concurrently; that is a security-boundary policy choice rather than a pure mechanical fix.

options.title: Accept locked reload-and-merge after proof
options.body: This preserves additive allow-always writes while avoiding stale whole-file overwrite, but requires live proof that admin revocations are not restored.

options.title: Require evaluated-hash CAS
options.body: This is stricter for concurrent admin changes, but it may intentionally skip some legitimate allow-always metadata or additive approval writes.

options.title: Pause for a narrower fix
options.body: This keeps the PR open while maintainers choose whether to fix only metadata writeback or the broader allow-always persistence race together.

recommendation.title: Accept locked reload-and-merge after proof
recommendation.body: This preserves additive allow-always writes while avoiding stale whole-file overwrite, but requires live proof that admin revocations are not restored.
